messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency spike for customer 'SolarBurst' on prod-region-us-east-1 · metric: inference.p99_latency = 2600ms (baseline 220ms) · affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream · triggered at 2026-03-15T10:00:00Z
oncall-amber: on call, looking. assigning SRE + runtime. @sre-miguel @eng-runtime-zoe please triage.
sre-miguel: Ack. pulling p95/p99 dashboards now.
eng-runtime-zoe: I'm at logs. seeing a big rise in streaming stalls and many long prefix requests from SolarBurst IP block. KV cache eviction rate jumping.
sre-miguel: quick numbers: p95 ~ 520ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 220ms -> 2.6s for the tenant's shard. Global p99 only up 10%. looks single-tenant.
support-nina: CS: SolarBurst noticed degraded streaming for ~5% of sessions starting ~09:58Z, but our telemetry shows backlog since ~09:55Z. customers reporting partial responses / reconnects.
cs-james: I've opened a customer-facing incident note and told them we're investigating with priority. they have high fanout usage during business ops.
eng-runtime-zoe: Observed pattern: repeated long shared prefix (~4k tokens) across many concurrent requests causing long KV lookups and large attention windows. Also their concurrency from a single API key jumped from 40 -> 420 RPS in last 3 mins.
sre-miguel: queue depth on the tenant's serving pool is high. single-tenant pool pinned to 3 GPU workers. latency correlation: high queueing + KV cache thrash = tail blowup.
infra-ops-rahul: checking autoscaler logs. tenant pool didn't autoscale because reserved capacity hit and autoscaler cooldown prevented new workers.
oncall-amber: mitigation plan: 1) temporary rate-limit SolarBurst to reduce tail 2) route overflow to spare pool/region 3) increase pool capacity if possible 4) engineer to investigate KV eviction policy tuning. who can do (2)+(3)? @rahul @zoe
infra-ops-rahul: can try vertical bump: kubectl scale deploy/serving-solarburst --replicas=6 -n prod (from 3) but might take 30-45s to warm. kicking now.
eng-runtime-zoe: starting routing change: will set routing fallback to multi-tenant spare pool for new requests from SolarBurst, keep existing sessions sticky. command: ```rdwctl route set --customer solarburst --fallback spare-pool-us-east --mode gradual```
sre-miguel: applying soft rate limit at the API gateway for that API key: ```gatewayctl policy attach --api-key SB_KEY_*** --rate 250rps --burst 50``` will cap short-term fanout while we scale.
support-nina: noted — telling customer we applied short-term throttling to stabilize and reduce reconnects. giving ETA 10-15m for visible improvements.
eng-runtime-zoe: after routing change: new requests are flowing into spare-pool, initial success. p99 for the tenant's new sessions dropped to ~900ms. old sticky sessions still showing stalls.
sre-miguel: checking streaming stall metric (stream.stall_rate): went from 0.3% -> 6.8% at spike peak. now down to ~1.7% for overall, but tenant-specific still ~3.5%.
infra-ops-rahul: scaled serving-solarburst replicas to 6. node utilization moderate. warming KV caches.
oncall-amber: good. next steps: keep throttles in place, continue to monitor p95/p99 across both pools. if stalls persist, consider model variant fallback (shorter context) for new requests.
eng-runtime-zoe: investigating KV cache eviction logs. seeing repeated evictions correlated with requests that share a long rare prefix token pattern. that causes cache churn because prefix keys are unique per session. hypothesis: prompt fanout + unique long prefix -> ineffective prefix caching.
sre-miguel: mitigation idea: enable per-tenant prefix dedupe + increase kvcache size for that pool. landing change may be risky now. prefer short-term: failover more traffic to spare pool where kvcache warm and less thrash.
cs-james: customer impact summary for timeline note: ~09:55-10:05Z severe tail impacted ~40% of their streaming sessions; after mitigations at 10:02Z partial recovery; ongoing degradation for legacy sessions until 10:12Z.
support-nina: customer acknowledged and appreciates the temporary throttle. asked for ETA on permanent mitigation. will follow up after postmortem.
eng-runtime-zoe: rolling a canary change to route new requests to a context-limited model variant (model-x-32k -> model-x-8k) for that API key to test tail impact: ```rdwctl model pin --customer solarburst --model model-x-8k --mode canary --pct 30```
sre-miguel: monitoring effect: canary p99 ~ 650ms for those cohorts. looks promising.
oncall-amber: leave throttle + gradual routing for 20 more mins. if stable, we'll remove throttle and keep model fallback as mitigation for heavy prefixes.
infra-ops-rahul: once stable we should patch autoscaler cooldown logic so reserved capacity doesn't prevent emergency scale for pinned tenants. filing follow-up ticket: INF-2026 (autoscaler cross-tenant emergency path).
sre-miguel: created incident ticket INC-2026-SOLARBURST with timeline, root-cause hypothesis, mitigations and owners.
eng-runtime-zoe: logs snippet for debug: ```[2026-03-15T09:59:58Z] key=SB_KEY_123 req_id=abc123 prefix_hash=0x7f9e evict_rate=0.74 cache_entries=1200/2048 queue_len=42 worker=serving-3```
sre-miguel: final note: primary root cause likely combination of sudden high concurrency from single API key + long unique prefixes causing KV cache thrash on a small, pinned single-tenant pool. mitigations applied: rate limit, routing overflow, temporary replica bump, canary model fallback. Postmortem to cover autoscaler, kvcache tuning, and customer-side guidance on request fanout.
oncall-amber: thanks team. I'll hand off to postmortem owners and close paging. :white_check_mark:
